# CopyMessage Unknown-Field Troubleshooting Tree

When BOT-219 resurfaced, the most useful item was still the original, narrowly scoped record: run CopyMessage Unknown Field Tolerance through the public entry point, and record only what this specific path actually returns or throws. The symptom described in the card was that the output could not be reliably reproduced. It did not specify the names of the unknown fields or their nesting level, nor did it provide an input that could be used directly as a regression sample.

This troubleshooting page preserves that incomplete state. It was once used to explain an interface compatibility issue, so it will still be referenced; however, its original approach of pointing to the polls file can no longer be followed as-is. The branches below are intended to make the result of an observed run specific enough to retain, while avoiding treating an unconnected source location as a fix location.

---

### The approach left by the initial draft

The May record linked the issue name and the call name to:

`telegrambots-meta/src/main/java/org/telegram/telegrambots/meta/api/methods/polls/SendPoll.java`

The assessment at the time was written as "Start with `JsonIgnoreProperties` to see whether unknown fields are silently dropped." This assessment had no accompanying call snippet and no consistently reproducible run; it was only a search order. The file header was indeed visible:

```java
package org.telegram.telegrambots.meta.api.methods.polls;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonIgnoreProperties;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonProperty;
import lombok.AllArgsConstructor;
```

These lines remained worth retaining later, because they explain why the investigation started here: this location looked like the definition of a API method with JSON mappings. However, imports are not behavior. They do not show that `JsonIgnoreProperties` is applied to the relevant type, do not show the annotation's specific configuration, and certainly do not prove that CopyMessage reads and writes objects here.

The old record's instruction to "change the ignore policy first, then try again" no longer applies. Until the direct relationship between CopyMessage and this file is confirmed, do not adjust annotations or object construction on SendPoll. Even if such a change stops an ad hoc input from producing an error, that does not show that it addresses the original issue.

---

### Start from the public entry point

First, run only the public entry point indicated by BOT-219; do not mix in similar sending methods, poll requests, or other JSON samples. Once a run ends, use the tree below to choose the next step.

```text
Run CopyMessage Unknown Field Tolerance
|
+-- Returned content is obtained
|   |
|   +-- The returned content is consistent
|   |   Record the object in the input that contains the unknown field, the returned content, and the number of consecutive runs;
|   |   do not write "all unknown fields are accepted" just because there is no exception.
|   |
|   +-- The returned content is inconsistent
|       Retain the input and returned content from each run, and check whether the differences occur only outside the unknown fields;
|       if the differences cannot be isolated, stop drawing conclusions about tolerance behavior.
|
+-- An exception is thrown
|   |
|   +-- The exception occurs consistently
|   |   Save the full exception content, and indicate whether it occurred before the entry-point call, during the call, or after reading the result;
|   |   then look for the object definition connected to CopyMessage.
|   |
|   +-- The exception does not occur consistently
|       Record it as "not reproduced" for now, and do not attribute an individual exception to unknown fields.
|
+-- There is no clear return and no exception that can be saved
    Record whether the run ended and what was visible at the time; this branch cannot establish compatibility or incompatibility.
```

Here, "consistent" only means that the same kind of content can be obtained repeatedly in the current record. It is not a compatibility guarantee, nor does it cover all input shapes. In particular, do not describe a single empty result as a field being ignored: an empty result may occur outside the entry point, and BOT-219 does not provide enough detail to distinguish these cases.

If all that can be obtained from the observed case is "cannot be reliably reproduced," still note which branch it occurred in. Explicitly stating that there is no returned-content sample or no exception sample is more valuable than adding speculation. The investigation can pause at this level; there is no requirement to invent a field name or a substitute input just to complete the record.

---

### Link source locations to the object first

Once the public entry point has been recorded, check the old path. The order is not to infer behavior backward from annotations, but first to confirm whether CopyMessage actually passes through this location.

```text
Confirm the relationship between CopyMessage and SendPoll
|
+-- A direct declaration, call, or explicit reference is found
|   |
|   +-- The reference is near field mapping
|   |   Check whether the actual declaration uses the JSON annotation; record the type or field carrying the annotation,
|   |   and do not bring other imports from the same file into the conclusion.
|   |
|   +-- The reference only passes through a shared base class, a construction path, or another adjacent location
|       Retain that adjacent location and continue following the actual references; do not modify SendPoll just because both belong to methods.
|
+-- No direct relationship is found
|   Remove SendPoll from the fix candidates for this investigation; retain the old path only as a historical misreading.
|
+-- The current material is insufficient to determine the relationship
    Stop the record at "relationship unconfirmed," and do not infer where the implementation belongs from the package name.
```

`package org.telegram.telegrambots.meta.api.methods.polls;` only indicates the package containing the file. For CopyMessage, it is a potentially misleading adjacent location, not a confirmed implementation entry point. The old record placed "method API" and "polls package" in the same search chain as a convenience to locate the issue quickly at the time; they must be separated during review.

Treat the three visible imports in the same way:

- Seeing `JsonIgnoreProperties` only means that this file may need declarations related to the JSON ignore policy. Until its actual use on the target type is seen, this is not grounds for concluding that unknown fields are accepted.
- Seeing `JsonProperty` only means that name mapping may exist. Field-name mapping and unknown-field handling are two different things and cannot substitute for each other.
- When seeing `AllArgsConstructor`, do not conflate constructor generation with deserialization behavior. If the issue with CopyMessage manifests as an object-creation failure, the object and path where it occurs still need to be confirmed first.

If the direct relationship ultimately leads elsewhere, the old path does not need to be deleted. There are two reasons to retain it here: it explains why some older investigations started with SendPoll; it also prevents the next person who sees the same imports from treating them as a conclusion again. Just do not treat this file as the default location to modify anymore.

---

### Keep the parts of the observed record separate

A failure record should be split into at least the following parts, to avoid putting the input state and source-code guesses in the same sentence:

```text
Entry point: CopyMessage Unknown Field Tolerance
Input for this run: the object level at which the unknown field appears; if it cannot be confirmed, write unconfirmed explicitly
How it ended: return / exception / no clear content
Verbatim content retained: returned content or exception content
Repeat runs: whether the same input was run again; if it was not repeated, do not add speculation
Source check: the relationship between CopyMessage and SendPoll is confirmed / unconfirmed / not found
```

"Input for this run" does not need to be turned into a general-purpose example. BOT-219 did not retain a field name, and inventing one would lead later readers to believe it came from the original observed case. If all you have is an entry-point description, retain that description; if you can confirm that the unknown field is in a nested object, record only that level of detail.

Do not replace "How it ended" with "success," either. Returned content does not imply semantic correctness, and an exception does not imply field rejection. Keep the actual returned or thrown content in place so that later readers can determine whether two records describe the same phenomenon. For a run with no clear content, simply record the fact that the run ended; do not fill it in as an empty response, a timeout, or a server-side rejection.

"Repeat runs" only answers whether the run was repeated and whether the result was the same. Do not extrapolate a single, unrepeated result into a probability judgment. The original issue was precisely that it could not be reliably reproduced; the record format should make this gap stand out, rather than conceal it behind a smoothly worded conclusion.

---

### Stopping points when similar symptoms appear

Some observed cases mention CopyMessage, other method objects, and the JSON annotation together. Their names are similar, but this page only addresses CopyMessage Unknown Field Tolerance. Limit the scope as follows:

```text
A similar method or a similar JSON type appears
|
+-- It can be proven to participate in the current entry point for CopyMessage
|   Continue recording its relationship to the returned content or exception from this run.
|
+-- It was mentioned only because its name is similar
|   Do not include it in this investigation's result, and do not modify annotations on that basis.
|
+-- It is another field or constructor visible in SendPoll
    Unless a direct reference already exists, retain it only as a historical navigation aid, not as a fix target.
```

This stopping point applies especially to the polls file. Its filename, package name, and imports are enough to support reading the code, but not enough to support a compatibility fix. If the investigator has already obtained a declaration directly connected to CopyMessage, the old path in this record should be treated as a side path; do not detour back to SendPoll just to make the historical page look complete.

Do not expand unknown-field tolerance into "a unified policy for all unknown content in JSON," either. This page provides no cross-object comparisons and no results for inputs at different nesting levels. It serves only to review the current entry point.

---

### Later addendum: the rollback action did not establish a conclusion

BOT-219 was marked as `rollback_checked` in the follow-up actions. This means that the rollback option was examined, not that a rollback was performed, and not that a rollback resolved the inability to reproduce the issue reliably. Someone previously treated this marker as supporting evidence that "the old behavior has been restored"; that interpretation should be crossed out.

After checking rollback, still return to the entry-point record:

```text
Seeing rollback_checked
|
+-- Public entry-point records from before and after rollback are available
|   Compare whether the returned content or exceptions on both sides are of the same kind; if a difference appears in only one run, retain the difference without classifying it.
|
+-- Only an action marker is available
|   State explicitly that only the check is confirmed; a behavior change cannot be inferred from the marker.
|
+-- The entry point itself still cannot be reliably reproduced
    Do not list rollback as a recovery action; keep the issue in the not-reproduced state.
```

This addendum corrects the recording method, rather than making a new determination about interface behavior. It does not supply versions from before and after rollback, does not supply returned-content samples, and does not establish fixed conditions for the original unknown-field issue. Therefore, this page continues to retain "the output cannot be reliably reproduced" as the description of the observed case, rather than rewriting it as a closed compatibility defect.

---

### Minimum results for handoff

There is no need to complete every branch when finishing an investigation. Any of the following three endings is acceptable:

1. **Consistent returned content or a consistently occurring exception was obtained.** Retain the verbatim content, and state whether the source relationship is confirmed or still unconfirmed. Only the former leads to discussion of a specific implementation location.
2. **Results remain inconsistent across multiple runs.** Retain how each run ended and the known input nesting levels, and mark the results as inconsistent; do not attach recommended changes.
3. **There is not enough material to confirm the relationship between the entry point and SendPoll.** Stop after reviewing the old path. This is a cleaner result than continuing to speculate about imports.

The initial draft treated "the JSON annotation can be found" as sufficient reason for the next step; now it is only a possible lead for reading the code. If any of the public entry-point record for BOT-219, the actual returned content or exception, or the direct source relationship of CopyMessage is missing, the apparent proximity of the polls file must not be used in its place.

This page still retains the old path and assessments so readers can see why the historical investigation turned to SendPoll. When implementation changes are needed, first obtain a fresh record of the current entry point; do not modify the file directly based on the initial draft here.

# Object Model Compatibility History

The initial draft in May addressed just one small point: it did not collapse the three objects in the title into a single "decoding issue". At the time, some preferred to start with Message because it already had a clear file location; the other view was that the file location could only explain the immediate connections around Message, not establish where the transaction partner or BotDescription belonged. The initial draft adopted the latter approach, but its wording still read much like a master checklist waiting to be filled in.

The original assessment is retained below: `telegrambots-meta/src/main/java/org/telegram/telegrambots/meta/api/objects/message/Message.java` is the reference point for revisiting Message Identifier Decoding Compatibility. This assessment was not removed because it did allow troubleshooting to return to the object declaration; however, it is no longer treated as the common entry point for all three topics.

Very few source code snippets were recorded at the time:

```java
public class Message implements MaybeInaccessibleMessage {
```

The location given in the index is `Message(type, line 84)`. The file is in the `org.telegram.telegrambots.meta.api.objects.message` package, and its header directly imports `JsonIgnore`, `JsonIgnoreProperties`, and `JsonProperty`. These details only show that the checks began with the message object file; they do not provide the complete process for handling identifiers across input types. Early drafts placed annotations too close to "compatibility is already complete", and a later review separated those ideas.

## The consolidated write-up that was not adopted

One approach considered was to organize the three topics around a shared closeout step: first locate `Message.java`, then list both the affiliate program transaction partner and the BotDescription builder as deserialization objects of the same kind. The advantage was that reviewers would only need to look at one file, and the record would be short. The problem was that, in the available material, only Message had a class declaration and a file-level location; the transaction partner concerned an inventory of dependents, while BotDescription concerned checks of the call entry point and results. They had different subjects to investigate.

The decision retained was therefore not "all issues have been resolved individually", but to separate the record by evidence type: the object file still belongs under Message; issues concerning dependents do not borrow Message's path; builder issues follow the caller. This boundary was the first substantive decision finalized on this page.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    state "Three topics recorded side by side" as listed
    state "Message file checks" as message
    state "Inventory of transaction partner dependents" as partner
    state "BotDescription entry point and result checks" as description
    state "Retain the file-level reference point" as retained
    state "caller_walkthrough" as walkthrough

    [*] --> listed
    listed --> message
    listed --> partner
    listed --> description
    message --> retained
    description --> walkthrough
```

The branches in the diagram are not an implementation call graph. They simply separate the three lines of verification retained in this decision record: Message has a file-level location, the affiliate program transaction partner must first address its dependents, and the BotDescription builder cannot skip the entry point and results. The initial draft's reference to "unified closeout" remains above to explain why that approach was not developed further later on.

## Message: retain the file location, narrow the conclusion

The review returned once again to `Message.java`. The only details that could be reliably restated were the class declaration, package name, and Jackson-related imports. They are enough to include Message in the object model checks, and enough to explain why the old troubleshooting records pointed from issue names and call names to this file.

There had previously been a shortcut inference: since `Message(type, line 84)` already pointed to the class declaration, record "Message Identifier Decoding Compatibility" as something the file already covered. This inference was not adopted. A class declaration is not an input sample, and annotation imports are not a comparison of results; directly documenting the two as completed compatibility work would mislead later readers into thinking that records of specific behavior had already been seen.

The decision retained here is to treat the path as a starting point for tracing back, not to elevate it into a conclusion. To continue tracking differences in Message's current results, `BOT-215` leads back to the corresponding item. The observation behind that card's creation was differences in the current version's results, making it a suitable place to take up user paths not yet covered; this page only retains why the file location was not recorded as the final assessment at the time.

## Transaction partner: do not borrow a neighboring object when no object location is available

Affiliate Program Transaction Partner Decoding was the easiest part of the initial draft to misread. With the three topics appearing consecutively, readers would naturally treat it as a variant of Message, or assume that the message object path in `telegrambots-meta` already established the transaction partner's dependency relationships. The existing records support neither claim.

The direction retained in `BOT-220` is an "inventory of current dependents": rerun the corresponding entry point on platforms supported by the maintainer, and check the files and versions actually generated. It did not provide a transaction partner class name, generated filename, or passing result that could be included on this page. The review therefore rejected the proposal to add it to the Message section.

This decision is intentionally presented as incomplete. Retaining only Message's source code snippet would strip this history of the context in which all three items entered closeout together; describing the transaction partner as already mapped to the same object would disguise dependents still awaiting an inventory as confirmed relationships. The current version still retains the name and direction of work, but does not fill in an object mapping that has not been established.

## BotDescription: a walkthrough was added to the record, but no results were fabricated

After October, the BotDescription builder item gained a record of a `caller_walkthrough` action. It shows that the review had followed the caller through once, and explains why v2 no longer just says "entry point still to be found". But the action itself did not include a failure stage, download artifacts, or a passing result, so it cannot be used to judge the builder or deserialization work complete.

The write-up for this item therefore differs from the initial draft, but the conclusion remains restrained: check the entry point and results separately. `BOT-224` leads back to the current entry point and result checks; the card requires the failure stage and downloadable artifacts to be recorded separately, preserving exactly why these two fields have not yet appeared on this page. This page does not turn the walkthrough into a passing test, nor treat "builder" as shorthand sufficient to establish deserialization behavior.

This addition also corrected a statement in the initial draft. The draft said that BotDescription "needed the actual call entry point to be found", which is no longer entirely accurate: a walkthrough action already exists. A more accurate account in the old record would be that the entry-point investigation had been walked through, but the results still had not produced material that could be restated on this page. The old sentence remains in version one so that later readers can see exactly what this change added.

## Decision after review

The review actually compared two maintenance costs. Combining the three items into one unified compatibility conclusion would look tidy in the short term, but any subsequent change in one object's results would force a rewrite of the entire page; recording them along three distinct lines of verification makes the page asymmetric, but preserves the distinction between known and unknown facts. The latter was chosen.

The resulting statuses are also asymmetric:

- Message continues to retain the file-level reference point and class declaration;
- The affiliate program transaction partner remains at the inventory of dependents, waiting for the actual entry point to produce files and versions that can be checked;
- The BotDescription builder retains the caller walkthrough, while the results still require separate confirmation.

Separating the three does not mean they are no longer related. They still belong to the same round of API compatibility closeout, and all should avoid prematurely turning object names, filenames, or action names into conclusions about behavior. This historical decision record simply does not take on the responsibility of filling in implementation details for all three.

Finally, one previously rejected proposal is retained: open the document with Message's object location, then close all three topics with the same "deserialization compatibility" wording. That proposal was abandoned not because the Message path lacked value, but because it would obscure the transaction partner's dependent-side issues and the gap in results for BotDescription. Investigation can still continue separately from `BOT-215`, `BOT-220`, and `BOT-224`, but when returning to this page, the boundary retained here should govern: the same round of closeout does not mean the same implementation entry point.

# Meta Caller Alternative Route Proposal

This page has been kept because people still follow the old link and ask why splitting out a custom endpoint was discussed at the time. It records a caller integration path that was not adopted, not the current integration instructions. The scope of the comparison in the early text was narrow, and the entry-access issues added later were not backfilled into the first version.

## Initial split

There were initially only two candidates: continue with `multipart sending`, or split out `custom endpoint` separately. The draft then leaned toward splitting because the two paths diverged at different points when they failed. That rationale only shows that two failure exits were seen at the time; it does not establish that they came from the same object, the same permissions, or the same caller.

The first version also included a very rough trial idea: keep the same users, inputs, and observation window on both sides, and first store the original input, version, and first result observed. The candidate side planned to try `polymorphic object decoding`; during recovery, it should be possible to return to `JSON round trip`. That wording was left unchanged because it explains why the later review asked about comparison conditions, but it does not mean the trial had started.

Two things were omitted at the time. First, the actual callers involved in cross-module regression were not listed; second, if the candidate path encountered a non-null constructor contract, unknown-field compatibility, or `builder validation`, the original "split out the endpoint" was no longer the only variable. The old draft lumped all of these into the exit criteria, making the assessment too optimistic.

## Entry Issues Seen Later

BOTA-004 was later followed by a reminder about the timing of the current-entry change: metrics from before and after the change cannot be subtracted directly. The access record retained on the card is also more specific—when the exit entry was viewed from the regular entry, the second step was denied; `qa-reader` at the exit entry was still 403, and the request ID remains on the card. This failure is first of all an access restriction; it cannot be used to judge the relative merits of the sending method and object decoding.

As a result, the two-week comparison in the second version needs a prerequisite check: whether each of the current entry, original revision, and exit entry is accessible. Results from the three locations must not be conflated. The public entry must be rechecked against the original `telegrambots-meta-client-integration`; local results may only aid diagnosis. If neither the current entry nor the original revision has a result, the handling for BOTA-015 is to keep it unknown, rather than fill the gap with one green build.

An offline Maven build was also once included among the preparation items. At most, it shows that that build could complete offline; it cannot replace verification of the caller path. The first version put this kind of check in the same section as actual caller integration testing, making it easy to think that a passing build already supported the split approach; that assessment no longer applies.

## Review Objections

The review did not accept the inference "the failure exits are different, so they should be split." First, verify whether the dual-state `telegrambots-meta-client-integration` referred to by BOTA-005 is the same object; if the objects have not been confirmed, comparing the two states is meaningless. BOTA-006 also calls for verification at the public entry, precisely to avoid treating a local observation as a caller-side conclusion.

Another issue was the rollback method. The old draft asked only "whether to restore the old entry"; it did not ask who would handle calls still pointing to the old entry after restoration. BOTA-014 later recorded the maintenance entry and the actual person taking over separately: the decommissioned group should be removed from the new entry. This addendum did not define a new long-term division of responsibility; it only says that rolling back the old plan cannot be done by changing a single address.

Therefore, the withdrawal conditions on this page should be read as part of the proposal as it stood at the time:

1. When the access status of the current entry, original revision, and exit entry cannot be confirmed separately, do not compare trends;
2. When verification at the public entry is incomplete, do not use local results to decide whether to retain the candidate;
3. If `JSON round trip` cannot be restored after exit, the candidate route stops;
4. When the dual-state objects have not been checked and the cross-module callers have not been clearly listed, do not write the split as an established migration.

These conditions were stop points written at the time to avoid expanding the trial, not general release rules established later.

## The Conclusion Remains at This Point

The route that was not adopted was to split `custom endpoint` out of the existing calls and use `polymorphic object decoding` as the candidate integration surface. It was not proven wrong by a single 403 record, nor proven feasible by a successful offline Maven build; both interpretations go beyond the source material.

This page can be viewed together with BOTA-004, BOTA-005, BOTA-006, BOTA-014 and BOTA-015. The first one preserves the entry change and access interruption; the remaining items correspond respectively to object verification, public-entry verification, the maintenance entry, and the no-result state. # Meta Entry Point Migration Index

This page starts with the call-site context for `telegrambots-meta-client-integration`. The index contains one old entry point, one replacement location ready for trial use, and several side paths used only for validation. They were once documented together, but it later became clear that a single build result cannot substitute for caller migration, so they are now recorded separately by action.

## Assessments left by the old draft

The earliest draft treated `constructor non-null contract` and `offline Maven build` as two alternative ways to move forward. That assessment has been discarded. The former describes the conditions under which a caller enters an object, while the latter only indicates whether the offline build path worked; they expose different objects when they fail, so the latter cannot be used to close out the former.

At the time, the actual callers of `polymorphic object decoding` were not listed either; the draft only said "continue investigating through the current entry point first". That sentence remains in the history, but is no longer a basis for declaring the migration complete. If a caller's name was not recorded in this index, do not fill in a name from a similarly named directory.

## Separate the tracks first

```text
Old entry point recorded in the index
Current Entry Point Old Entry Point Migration Index
        │
        ├── Trial with a single real caller ──> Polymorphic object decoding
        │                         │
        │                         └── Compare round-trip results using JSON
        │
        └── Offline Maven build / builder validation
            Build-side records only, not a substitute for caller confirmation
```

`docs/adj-telegrambots-meta/migration/current-entry-point-legacy-entry-point-migration-index.md` is the entry point for looking up this set of objects in the current project. It is not the replacement location itself. The migration record must answer at least three questions: where access originally started, where access starts after the trial, and which caller still in use has actually gone through the replacement location. Without all three, keep the old entry point.

### Migration ledger

| Batch | Entry point change | Context to retain | Stopping condition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Single-caller trial | Move from the old entry point registered in the index to `polymorphic object decoding` | Original input, version, first result, second-call status | That caller confirms the replacement location is usable |
| Result comparison | Keep the old entry point, then compare the `JSON round trip` | Successful results, errors, and discrepancies in their original form | The differences between the two sides' results can be explained, or a decision is made to roll back |
| Build-side check | Run the `offline Maven build` separately | Build output and failure exits | Report only the build status, without declaring the migration complete |
| Archive verification | Check the archive records for `telegrambots-meta-client-integration` | Last confirmable state; retain the captured context if no record can be found | The archive status is explicitly recorded |

A "single-caller trial" does not mean switching all integrating parties over at once. Select only one real user for the first batch, keep the old entry point readable, and do not delete the old route in advance. If the batch name and caller were not both recorded, the ledger can only go into this level of detail; do not fill in the blanks as completed.

## Procedure

### 1. Freeze a copy of the input before migration

Obtain an actual `telegrambots-meta-client-integration` input from the current index, and retain it together with the version and the first visible result. The records in BOTA-016 already explain that a newly fabricated, similar-looking input cannot replace a replay; the original input must continue to be used in subsequent comparisons and rollbacks.

First confirm that the old entry point can still read the same material. The regular entry point and the internal results may not be at the same layer: an existing record says "The internal results contain Current Result, but the regular entry point corresponding to Exit Entry Point does not." Therefore, when opening the regular entry point produces no result, do not immediately conclude that the replacement location has failed, and do not copy the internal results over as the regular entry point's results. Record the missing item as a gap, and continue checking against the original input.

### 2. Switch only one caller

Point one caller that is still in use to `polymorphic object decoding`, without changing other callers at the same time or mixing the `offline Maven build` into the same result. Record the entry point names before and after the switch, the version used, and the second-call status. Retain the original errors during comparison; cleaned-up screenshots or summaries cannot replace failure exits.

If the replacement location can return a result, but the second-call status differs from that of the old entry point, pause the batch at the comparison stage. Distinguish three cases here: no result on the first call, a result on the first call but failure on the second, and success on both calls but inconsistent content. Check all three against the original input; do not label them all as "compatible".

### 3. Check adjacent records

After the caller comparison passes, check the archive status. The work documented in BOTA-008 was once blocked because the shared test environment was temporarily unavailable; this kind of blocker can only postpone the batch, and the appearance of a new entry point in the directory cannot substitute for the check. Follow `telegrambots-meta-client-integration` to find the archive records, record the last confirmable state if found, and retain the original captured context if they are missing; do not mark an empty result as archived.

Open a separate record for the build side. The `offline Maven build` and `builder validation` each have their own failure exits, and a successful build only proves that this side passed. It does not prove that `polymorphic object decoding` has been adopted by a real caller, nor that the regular entry point now displays the same content as the internal results.

### 4. When to stop

Only after all three conditions are met—the replacement location can actually be called, the migrated caller has confirmed it, and historical lookups can still find the version used for this migration—can retirement of the old entry point be scheduled. If there is only build output or a single successful result, keep the old entry point.

Maintenance records still belong to `telegrambots meta · Client Integration`. The separate schedule, maintainer, and exit actions must remain in this set of objects' own records. When the work crosses into another project or interface, stop here; do not merge results from adjacent projects into this batch.

## Rollback is not deletion

If any of the following occurs, restore the old entry point first:

- The `JSON round trip` results are inconsistent, and the differences still cannot be explained;
- The second call fails, even though the first returned a result;
- The caller has not yet confirmed the replacement location;
- Archive records are missing, making it impossible to confirm which version is currently in use.

When restoring, reuse the original input saved before migration and go through the old entry point again. Record the first visible result and the second-call status before and after restoration. Do not just delete the reference to the new entry point; BOTA-017 also requires removing actions that point to the old exit action, while retaining the pre-change routing snapshot. The snapshot is a reference for comparison after rollback, not a new migration input.

The exit action recorded in BOTA-007 is: contact the original owner before expiry, and if there is no reply, wrap up according to the existing exit action. It only addresses stalled exit actions and does not mean that caller migration is complete. If the exit action has already been deleted, inspect the pre-change routing snapshot before deciding whether to restore the old entry point; if the snapshot cannot be found, leave the state unchanged and do not rebuild the routes from memory.

After rollback, retain the trial records for `polymorphic object decoding`, and indicate whether the failure occurred during the entry point switch, result comparison, second call, or archive verification. The original input, version, and failure exits must not be overwritten by green results. Any later retrial should start from the same captured context; if the input or version has changed, record a separate batch rather than overwriting this rollback.

## Boundaries added later

The name `Current Entry Point Old Entry Point Migration Index` is both a navigation title and something that was once treated as the name of an entry point that could be replaced directly. The two uses must not be confused: finding the index in the directory only means it was successfully located; only a real caller successfully going through the replacement location shows that the migration action has produced a result.

"The regular entry point has no current result" alone is also not enough to conclude that a rollback is needed. First confirm the versions visible in the internal results, the exit entry point, and the regular entry point, then compare using the original input. If only the regular entry point's display is missing, the issue is on the result-presentation side; only if an actual call to the replacement location also fails should the batch be stopped and the old entry point restored. The current records have no finer-grained fields, so do not break this down into unverified causes.

Side paths with similar names are not automatically merged. Keep the integration feedback, adaptation boundaries, and call samples for `telegrambots-meta-client-integration` here; other pages can only serve as navigation and must not fill in caller results for this page. Related cards BOTA-007, BOTA-008, BOTA-016, BOTA-017 can be followed further to trace exit actions, archive status, original-input replay, and old-route cleanup.

## Old steps still retained

The old draft's sequence of "check the directory first, then announce that the new entry point is in effect" has been discarded, but the original sentence and the unresolved state at the time are not deleted, because they explain why the process later changed to retaining the input and version first. The early proposal to separate out the `offline Maven build` is also retained; it can serve as a build-check batch, but cannot carry out caller migration.

There is currently no complete list of callers for `polymorphic object decoding`, nor enough material to break each compatibility case down into a separate result. For now, this record stops at the confirmed single-caller path, original-input replay, result comparison, and rollback actions. When adding a caller, add it to the corresponding batch; do not rewrite the first result of an old batch.

# Quality Signal Console Troubleshooting Tree

This page preserves an old on-call troubleshooting path for the Quality Signal Console: when a signal is not progressing from the `Current entry point`, first determine whether the incident state is still available, then decide whether the issue should remain in `telegrambots-abilities-quality-signal` or whether to stop and hand it off for an exit action or to the permissions owner. It was once used as a recovery runbook, but some of its checks applied only to the entry point used at the time. Do not treat the leaves of the tree as confirmed causes.

The old entry point is still at `docs/adj-telegrambots-abilities/runbooks/telegrambots-abilities-quality-signal-who-to-contact-when-stuck.md`. When taking over, start from the original entry point. Do not first switch entry points, rerun, or clean up the collated results; these actions create a new incident state but cannot recover material that was missing at the time of the first failure.

## Three steps left by the old version

The record from the year 2025 was brief and contained only this tree:

```text
Current entry point
└─ Find the custom endpoint
   ├─ Cross-module regression observed: preserve the incident state
   └─ Method path not present: stop
```

The focus then was `custom endpoint`, `cross-module regression`, and `method path`. These terms can still be used as search terms, but the old record did not establish a fixed causal relationship between them. In particular, "Method path not present" only means that the path was not seen in that record. It cannot automatically be equated with no execution, no permissions, or having already crossed an interface.

The old version also described "continue along this page" as if it were a sufficient recovery action. That wording can now be retained only as historical usage: no verification results were retained for the shared environment. The old page once included a practice of continuing troubleshooting after seeing a green result, but that was later withdrawn. A green rerun only means that the new run did not reproduce the issue; it does not supersede the first failing sample.

## First confirm whether the incident state is still available

Starting from the `Current entry point`, first ask whether the raw record exists. Here, the raw record must at least bring together the input, version, and first visible result in one place. A final status alone, a collated summary, or the result of a rerun cannot replace it.

```text
Visible symptoms at the current entry point
├─ No raw record for telegrambots-abilities-quality-signal
│  └─ Collect the missing data; stop here, without discussing root cause
└─ Raw record exists
   └─ Identify the first difference from the most recent normal sample
      ├─ The difference is still within the project's own resources, permissions, or indexes
      │  └─ Keep it within this project and hand it to the on-call maintainer
      └─ The difference crosses a clearly defined interface
         └─ Stop following this page and hand it to the shared owner
```

This is not a request to fill in a perfect log. The aim is to avoid reconstructing missing intermediate steps from the final display. If the original input was not saved, state that the input is unknown; if the version was not retained, state that the version is unknown; if the first result is incomplete, preserve that gap as well. Do not guess a revision just to make the record look continuous.

The action recorded in BOTB-002 addresses exactly this gap: fill in the current revision for the second run or read; if only the final status remains, leave it blank. This does not ask the on-call person to infer the version from elsewhere, nor does it mean that the second result can represent the first failure. The record in BOTB-008 is more direct: while collection or execution remains unconfirmed, the current revision remains unknown.

If the raw record does not exist, collect the missing data and then stop following this page. Any new sample that appears later should be treated as a new observation, not retroactively inserted as evidence that was already available in the old incident state. Do not continue attributing causes further down the tree merely because of the project name, directory name, or a normal-looking final page.

## How to compare when a sample is available

Once the raw record is available, identify only the first difference between `polymorphic object decoding` and the most recent normal sample. Do not replace the input, environment, and entry point at the same time; even if the result changes, you will not know which change caused it. Change only one condition per comparison.

The first difference cannot yet be called the root cause. It only determines what to examine at the next node: if it still concerns the Quality Signal Console's own resources, permissions, or indexes, keep it within the project; if it has crossed a clearly defined interface, do not continue using this page to infer behavior on the other side. If there is not enough material to choose between those two directions, stop at the first difference and retain the original and new samples side by side.

Averages, directory names, and the final display can all suggest where to look, but none substitutes for intermediate behavior. In particular, if a rerun turns green, do not use that as a reason to delete the failing input or reclassify the original failure as intermittent. One premature retry in the old record illustrates this lesson: afterward, the first failing sample was preserved before environment differences were collected.

## When `JSON round trip` appears

If the first difference occurs in `JSON round trip`, do not immediately label it a general compatibility issue. Distinguish between two cases:

- If the difference can still be explained by telegrambots abilities · Quality Signal Board's resources, permissions, or indexes, continue handling it within this project;
- If the difference requires changing the user-visible contract, or has already crossed a clearly defined interface, stop following this page and initiate a formal review.

"Stop" here does not mean abandoning the record. When stopping, retain the original input, version, first result, known environment differences, and the node where the tree stopped. Mark any missing item as unknown. This lets the person taking over know which part is missing, rather than conflating a permissions issue, a lack of execution records, and an interface change into a single "stuck" state.

The public record for 2026-01-30 says only that the current results differ between the two environments and that the command has not yet been located. This material supports the conclusion that the environment difference remains unexplained; it does not support inventing a command or choosing either environment as the normal baseline. When the environment differs and the result disappears, still preserve what has already been observed on both sides before returning to the first difference, rather than declaring recovery successful.

The backfill requirement in BOTB-011 is to add the preceding step before the `Current entry point`, retaining the last confirmable state before the failure. Until that state has been filled in, do not continue tracing toward the call edge. Explanations of the call edge must be based on an entry point that was actually reached and a confirmable preceding state.

## Two local terms that can lead you astray

`multipart sending` and `builder validation` appeared in later incidents, but they are not mandatory checks on every pass. Let them advance the tree only when the corresponding records are actually present:

```text
Does the raw record exist?
├─ No: collect the missing data, stop
└─ Yes
   ├─ Only multipart sending is observed
   │  └─ Retain the input and first result; do not infer a compatibility conclusion
   ├─ Only builder validation is observed
   │  └─ First check permissions, resources, or indexes within the project
   └─ Neither is present
      └─ Return to the first visible difference
```

`multipart sending` only indicates that this local term appears in the record; it cannot, on its own, prove caller compatibility. Nor can `builder validation` bypass the raw record and directly become a permissions conclusion. The old version once used "caller compatibility" as an endpoint; this wording later appeared premature because it prematurely settled an interface assessment that had not yet been confirmed. When retaining the old text, do not treat it as the current conclusion.

Handle an absent `method path` in the same way: first check whether there is visible input, then check whether the path belongs to the current project. A missing path, a lack of permissions, and no execution are not the same phenomenon and cannot share a single handoff conclusion.

## Handoff traces added later

BOTB-008 was marked as `release_classified` on 2026-01-14. This only shows that the card was classified, not that the incident had recovered. BOTB-002 moved into review on 2026-01-19, with the stated reason that the implementation had been completed on an existing branch; this status likewise cannot retroactively prove that the original failure had been explained.

On the same day, samples were attached to BOTB-005. After the samples entered the record, BOTB-005 was reassigned to the actual maintainer on 2026-01-20; the previous assignee was responsible only for triage. What can be confirmed here is that the samples and handoff relationships changed, not any additional cause of the failure. BOTB-011 underwent a documentation review on day 26 of month 1, while BOTB-008 did not move to In Progress until day 28 of month 1; neither a documentation review nor the start of work substitutes for a preserved execution from the incident.

Another requirement in BOTB-005 is to have someone who was not involved in the change follow the original steps, using the original author's results only for comparison. This requirement applies to branches that already have the original steps and samples; without a raw record, a fresh rerun cannot be passed off as a review by someone other than the author. BOTB-014 instead requires the person taking over to start from the original entry point of the `Current entry point` and note the first place where additional permissions are needed.

If the first point is a permissions gap, the tree stops at permissions. Do not infer that the call succeeded from a later displayed result, and do not treat the project name as indicating permissions ownership. The permissions owner enters this branch only when a permissions gap is actually observed.

## What to include in a handoff

If the difference still points to this project's own resources, permissions, or indexes, and the first failing sample, version, and first result are all still available, keep handling it within the project. If the difference can no longer be explained by these visible objects, or requires changing the user-visible contract, stop following this page and hand it to the shared owner.

Include the handoff material that is available: the original input, version, first result, environment differences, and stopping point. Explicitly mark missing items as unknown; do not fill them in using directories, averages, or later green results. This gives the shared owner a bounded difference rather than a story already filled with guesses.

`telegrambots-abilities-quality-signal` is an object involved in the incident, not an automatically assigned owner. DOC-34 records another segment of an incident involving the same Quality Signal Console and cannot be used to fill in results missing from this page. To revisit specific backfilled records, samples, or entry-point handoffs, consult the respective records at BOTB-002, BOTB-005, BOTB-008, BOTB-011, and BOTB-014.

This page still retains the old tree because it can remind the person taking over not to keep making assumptions when the `method path` is missing. If the user-visible behavior of `JSON round trip` needs to change later, record the formal review outcome separately; do not rewrite the record to say that an ordinary retry resolved it.

# Client Dual-State Anomaly Postmortem

The performance lab's current entry point reported different current revisions across two checks. The same experiment was shown both times, and the capacity baseline and resource curves had not been swapped out; only the version referenced by the entry point had changed. The first issue to surface was not a throughput drop: when the review continued from the old record, the method path no longer matched.

The working assumption at the time was still that "the entry point represents the latest rerunnable state." That assumption was never removed from the original record afterward: the entry-point change was treated as part of normal lab switching, not as a state divergence that needed its own explanation. As a result, the follow-up investigation continued along the old method path until the request context could no longer be matched to the version at the entry point.

## Incident timeline

- At the first check, the method path in the old record could still be used as the starting point for the capacity baseline.
- When the current entry point was opened again, the displayed current revision had changed; the resource curves remained under the original experiment.
- After further checks along the original path, it was possible to restore multipart sending. This recovery only showed that this sending branch was usable again; it did not show that the entry point and all request branches were consistent.
- The cause of the custom endpoint change was not found. Further retries provided no new information to distinguish between the possibilities, so retries were stopped and the entry-point version at the time and the version in the original record were retained.

The main impact was on regression diagnosis: the same resource curve could be used to explain two different versions, and the capacity baseline could also be mistaken for one from the current entry point. For requests requiring a recheck by method path, the old record can only show what was observed before; it cannot stand in for the entry point's state for that check. The earlier wording that presented "multipart has been restored" as an overall recovery was too broad, but this page still retains that framing so later readers do not mistakenly think endpoint-side confirmation had already been completed at the time.

## Actions taken at the time

The original record, the recovery page, and the unconfirmed cause were retained separately. The brief walkthrough near the entry point is at DOC-38; this page preserves the assessment made when the anomaly occurred. At handoff, the requirement was to start again from the current entry point, not infer the version from the last line of successful output or conflate the exit action's fallback state with the entry-point change.

"offline Maven build" was recorded as the stopping point at the time: it was suitable for preserving a recoverable build result, but did not answer why the current entry point had been repointed. That stopping point was kept in use too long afterward, making it easy to assume the custom endpoint change had already been explained.

Still missing: the exact point in time between the two entry-point changes; whether the current revision was left over from an old cache, an old job, or some other switch; whether the exit action and the entry-point state share the same fallback condition.

# Performance Lab Exit Window Procedure

This checklist preserves how an exit window in the Performance Lab was handled. The page continued to be used later to find the entry point, but some of its stop points were appropriate only for the material state at that time: it cannot replace capacity assessment for a later window or release sign-off.

The old window had three notes in the margin: first look for `builder validation`; if you see `non-null constructor contract`, do not clear the scene on the spot; without an `offline Maven build`, stop. This passage was not deleted. At the time, it helped us avoid taking down the setup too early, but it placed too much weight on the constructor check; now it can only be treated as a local signal in the old record. It is not enough to show that the resource curve is normal or that the degradation has been located.

Window closeout starts with existing material, not with a verbal conclusion. The entry point remains:

`docs/adj-telegrambots-client/release/telegrambots-client-performance-lab-exit-window-checklist.md`

Once in, first confirm that the version retained for this round corresponds to the original input. Here, "original input" means the material that triggered this round of capacity observation, not a summary assembled later. If the page contains only the cleaned-up text and the input or version from that time cannot be found, leave the window marked in progress; do not add a version number just to make archiving easier.

1. **Retain the last visible result.**
   - [ ] In the closeout record, state whether the last thing seen was command output, a test log, a trace fragment, or a diff fragment.
   - [ ] It should still be clear that the result belongs to this round's telegrambots-client-performance-lab, rather than being similar output brought in from elsewhere.
   - [ ] If the last result appeared only after cleanup, label it as a post-cleanup supplement; do not fold it into the pre-exit state.

"Last visible" is not "last successful." When no conclusion has been reached on the capacity baseline, resource curve, or degradation localization, the last visible material may be a rejection path, an incomplete log, or just a short trace fragment. Such material can serve as part of the basis for exit because it shows where the window stopped; it must not be rewritten as a green result.

2. **Keep the project's two samples side by side.**
   - [ ] Retain one sample from the project's own success path.
   - [ ] Retain one sample from the project's own rejection path.
   - [ ] At least one of the two can be matched to this round's version, input, or last visible result.

This does not require rerunning the full capacity test. During closeout, only confirm that the samples are still there and that context has not been lost through reorganization, moving, or overwriting. A success path only shows that there was a period of normal operation; a rejection path only shows that the boundary was observed. The two samples cannot substitute for each other, much less be used to endorse the release result.

3. **Verify the exit action itself.**
   - [ ] The exit action has left a readable record that distinguishes "preparing to exit" from "already exited."
   - [ ] The exit action associated with adj-telegrambots-client is not recorded only in a lab-side note.
   - [ ] Material still in use has not been treated as archived material.

The old version took "seeing a checklist item" as a signal that cleanup could continue; keep this as a historical reminder. In practice, the exit action and cleanup are not the same thing. The former can be completed, while the latter should still wait until the last visible result, the samples, and the exit record have been put together. If cleanup has already started but the exit record is found to be missing, retract this round's exit marker, retain the material already left behind, and do not continue closing out the window.

4. **Stop at the gap when something is missing.**

If any one of the version, original input, or last visible result cannot be found, do not mark the window complete. First stop any further exit actions; change any completion statement already written back to pending confirmation; do not use new command output, reorganized logs, or a diff generated later to fill the old state. If there is only a success path and no rejection path, do not infer on your own that degradation localization is complete; the exit action record may be retained, but the capacity-baseline conclusion cannot be carried into the closeout note.

Conversely, if the exit action has been executed and the materials are still intact, the record should explicitly state: "Action executed; release conclusion not confirmed here." Whether the release succeeded is signed off separately by the corresponding owner. The Performance Lab checklist is responsible only for leaving this window in a reviewable state; it is not responsible for making decisions on behalf of other interfaces or callers.

One type of old record is easy to misread: when the page says "the project's own success path and one rejection path have been retained as samples," readers assume that both samples came from the same run. The original record did not guarantee that. When using this page later, you can only confirm that the samples exist and the material boundary of each; you cannot infer from this sentence that they can be compared directly. If a new comparison is needed, open a separate run record; do not overwrite the old window left here.

Before completing closeout, do one more small check: whether the current page still points to the Performance Lab entry point, whether the exit action for adj-telegrambots-client has its own record, and whether the last visible result is still there. If any one of the three is missing, stop; even if all three are present, that only means the materials can be archived, not that the resource curve is free of degradation.

When taking over, start by reviewing from the path above. Preserve the old stop points alongside the page, the success sample, and the rejection sample as-is; when the exit judgment needs to be changed, add a new record rather than rewriting the old window as the later version's release policy.

# Supply boundary troubleshooting tree

When the entry point opens but keeps spinning once you reach the current result, do not start by recording the on-screen symptom as the root cause. Here, the "current entry point" is the page or call entry point where the symptom is first seen; the "first result" is the earliest state left at that entry point by the same input attempt. First preserve the evidence from this attempt, then determine whether the issue is still within `telegrambots-longpolling-supply-boundary` or now falls within the scope of an exit action or the permissions owner.

The only incident evidence left by BOTE-002 is this one sentence:

> The exit entry point opens, but at the current result it keeps spinning.

This is enough to start triage, but not enough to show that the endpoint, constructor arguments, or decoder have already failed. The page may spin before the entry point is reached, or after the input has entered but without leaving a result that can be compared. Do not clear temporary resources just to attribute the cause quickly, and do not record a later green rerun as recovery of the first sample.

First collect the four immediately visible items: the original input, the version used, the first visible result, and the environment marker at the time. They should come from the same attempt. If the input came from a `multipart send`, preserve the original input from that send, not equivalent content reconstructed later; if the entry point has already passed through a `custom endpoint`, record the position of that endpoint branch, but do not treat it as proof that the response is correct.

```text
After opening the current entry point, is the first failing sample still available?
├─ No
│  ├─ Only the page text or final display remains
│  │  └─ Collect the missing evidence; stop here and do not discuss the root cause
│  ├─ Only the green result after a retry remains
│  │  └─ Preserve that result and record it separately as a retry; it cannot replace the original incident state
│  └─ The input can be found, but the version or first result is missing
│     └─ Fill in the missing items before continuing
└─ Yes
   ├─ The first difference already appears before or after the entry point
   │  └─ Stay within the project; check the entry point, resources, permissions, or index
   ├─ Everything matches upstream; a difference appears only near polymorphic object decoding
   │  └─ Compare before and after the JSON round trip to locate the first change
   └─ The difference has already crossed a clearly defined interface
      └─ Stop troubleshooting on this page; hand off to the owners on both sides of the interface
```

The "most recent normal sample" cannot be replaced with an average, nor can you pick a seemingly similar result based on directory names. It should support an item-by-item comparison with the current sample at the same entry point up to the first difference. Change only one condition at a time: if the input, version, entry point, and environment all change at once, the tree cannot drill down further. In that case, record "samples cannot be compared" and return to the branch for collecting missing evidence.

## The entry point is still within the project

When both the input and version are available, and the first difference occurs before the entry point itself, resource indexing, or permission checks, first follow `telegrambots-longpolling-supply-boundary` and keep the investigation within the project. This branch only establishes how far the incident progressed; it does not draw conclusions for adjacent modules.

```text
Can the samples within the project be compared?
├─ No
│  └─ Preserve the existing evidence; do not guess its source from the final page
└─ Yes
   ├─ The entry point did not reach the custom endpoint
   │  └─ Record the entry-point-side difference and leave it for the project maintainer to continue
   ├─ The custom endpoint was reached, but the multipart send has no first result
   │  └─ Preserve the input, version, and endpoint position; stop rerunning
   └─ A first result is available and differs from the normal sample
      └─ Write down the first difference and stop at this node pending confirmation
```

`custom endpoint` is a signpost here, not a diagnostic result. Seeing it only means that this branch is present in the current record; not seeing it does not justify concluding that the request never arrived. The entry point record and first result need to be examined together. If the entry point record is still available but the first result is not, preserve the entry point record and switch to evidence collection, rather than first cleaning up resources and trying again.

`multipart send` should not be treated as a complete call chain either. It is a location that the early records required checking: first confirm whether the current sample reached it, then confirm whether a first result was left there. If only the final display remains after the send, with no intermediate result, you cannot attribute "the page keeps spinning" directly to the send operation. When samples are insufficient, stop investigating at the gap after the send.

The constructor-arguments branch deals only with locally visible evidence. Older records placed "constructor non-null contract" alongside the incident evidence and later also mentioned `builder validation`, but the old page did not preserve a set of samples proving that the actual rejection occurred during construction. Therefore, the constructor non-null contract can only remind whoever takes over to check the builder's input; it is not an established cause of the current failure.

```text
Do we need to examine builder validation?
├─ The input was not preserved
│  └─ Do not judge the constructor arguments; return to collecting missing evidence
├─ The input is available, but the validation result was not preserved
│  └─ Record "pending confirmation"; do not fill in error output
└─ Both the input and validation result are available
   ├─ The difference is already present here: stay within the project
   └─ Everything matches here: continue comparing before and after the JSON round trip
```

An early draft described the route as "find `multipart send`, continue after seeing `custom endpoint`, and stop when `cross-module regression` appears". The gap in this sequence is that it pushes you to the next step even when no sample is available. Now, first ask whether the sample exists, then ask where its first difference from the normal record is. The old sequence is retained as a starting point for searching, but no longer serves as a condition for direct escalation.

## The difference has reached the JSON round trip

If the input before polymorphic object decoding still matches the normal sample, and the difference appears only around the JSON round trip (the process of serializing and then decoding), do not go back and substitute the final page state for the comparison. First preserve the original object and first result, then compare the content before and after the custom endpoint down to the first differing field or node.

```text
The samples have been preserved; on which side is the difference?
├─ Already different before the JSON round trip
│  └─ Return to the entry point, resource index, or builder validation
├─ Different only after the JSON round trip
│  └─ Stop at the serialization boundary; hand off to the corresponding owner
├─ The before-and-after content is available, but the first difference cannot be found
│  └─ Collect another input/output pair from the same entry point; do not overwrite it with a retry
└─ Only the final display is available
   └─ You cannot determine whether it passed through this boundary; return to evidence collection
```

In the former case, hand off to both sides of the interface; in the latter, go through a separate formal review; this page preserves the incident state and stopping point.

The record includes the environment marker "offline Maven build". It only indicates that troubleshooting took place under that build condition at the time; it cannot replace runtime samples or establish how the custom endpoint behaves in other environments. Whoever takes over should put it in the same record as the version, entry point, and first result; if the environment is unknown, explicitly mark it as unknown first rather than substituting the environment from another sample.

Retrying too early previously made the entry point display results again, and in doing so obscured the chronology and environmental differences of the original incident. ├─ The first sample has not yet been preserved
```text
│  └─ First stop further attempts and collect the missing evidence
├─ The first sample has been preserved, but the environment differs before and after the retry
│  └─ Record the two results separately; do not overwrite one with the other
├─ The retry turned green, but the first difference has not been located
│  └─ Still triage based on the first sample
└─ The issue has been located within the project or at an interface boundary

```

It means stopping the next operation and preserving the existing evidence when further attempts would lose the incident state, or when the situation is already beyond what this page can determine. If it stopped at the evidence-collection branch, specify whether the missing item is the input, version, first result, or environment; if it stopped at an internal project branch, specify whether the first difference was on the entry point, resource, permission, index, or builder side; if it stopped after the JSON round trip, attach the before-and-after samples. # Code-reading notes on the dependency cache maintenance entry point

This follow-up review was initially easy to turn into a search for the "cache implementation": the input contains api-methods-validation, and the repository also contains names related to methods, validation, and caching. In practice, the task was not to assign ownership of a same-named object, but to trace a call path during startup to where dependency cache maintenance first takes effect. The route still starts at the public entry point; the scope has not been expanded to all method models or all startup components.

First, put the objects at hand in the following order. The vertical lines in the diagram indicate the direct relationships that need to be confirmed in this pass; they do not mean that all objects in the same directory, with the same name, or appearing together in search results belong to this path.

```text
Public entry point for api-methods-validation
              |
              | Select one direct caller
              v
       Pass-through point during startup
              |
              v
       Dependency cache maintenance
              |
              | First actual use of the maintenance result
              v
          First real consumer
```

Keeping the public entry point for api-methods-validation as the starting point has two practical benefits. First, the person taking this over knows where to narrow the search, rather than pulling every unrelated implementation in under "cache." Second, later notes can answer directly, "Where does this caller come in from?" without guessing from filenames. The public entry point here is the entry point for this review, not a redivision of module responsibilities.

`telegrambots-meta/src/main/java/org/telegram/telegrambots/meta/api/methods/polls/SendPoll.java` used to appear early in the search results. It contains the adjacent terms api, methods, and validation, making it a suitable signpost back to the public entry point; during the later review, it was no longer recorded as the location of cache maintenance. A filename and path can show where this review started, but cannot by themselves show what it calls. Once this is clear, handling same-named files is straightforward: if the name matches but there is no call edge, leave it as a signpost and keep it out of the main path.

The starter startup log serves to locate things here. While reading, first find in the log the startup point where the selected caller appears, then return to that caller's direct relationship to confirm what it passes to the next segment. This is not about turning the log into a substitute for source code, but about avoiding back-and-forth among static search results. The log answers only, "Where did this section pass through during startup?"; the call relationship answers, "Who carried dependency cache maintenance onward?" If the two do not line up, preserve the inconsistency first; do not fill in a path that only appears continuous.

"Following only one direct caller" also needs a clear stopping point. Here, the direct caller is the node that can be confirmed to enter the next step from the public entry point, not every object that references the entry point's name. After selecting it, do not expand a second or third caller in parallel; otherwise this page becomes a complete code-reading note for api-methods-validation, and the person taking it over still will not know where the first actual path is. If that node merely passes parameters along, registers a callback, or stores a reference, it remains a pass-through point on the chain, not the consumer this page is looking for.

The first real consumer is determined by use: it must be the first object to use the result of dependency cache maintenance to continue with a subsequent action. Simply holding the object, passing it through unchanged, or being returned by a search solely because the name is similar does not count. This criterion separates "where maintenance is mentioned" from "when maintenance starts to affect subsequent behavior." After review, the main path stops at this consumer; calls further down are not expanded on this page unless they could in turn change the determination of the first consumer.

Earlier notes placed `SendPoll.java` too early, making it read as though it itself provided call evidence. That ordering was wrong. The path is retained so later readers know where the search entered; at the same time, it is explicitly returned to signpost status. Similarly, the starter startup log was previously treated as material that could directly connect the path; it is now used only to locate startup order. These two changes add no new caller and do not turn an unconfirmed same-named object into a dependency relationship.

At handoff, leave four short fields rather than reworking a large graph:

```text
Public entry point: api-methods-validation
Selected caller: one confirmed direct caller
Log location: corresponding startup segment in the starter startup log
First consumer: object that first actually uses the result of dependency cache maintenance
```

The object names in these fields should come from relationships already inspected during this pass; when uncertain, write "pending confirmation" rather than using a signpost file to fill the slot. Especially for the first consumer field, if the only evidence is that it was passed through, go back to the previous field and continue checking instead of relabeling the pass-through point as a consumer.
